leadRow.source: Primary / Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority / 2026-08-20

evidence.sourceTitle: Swiss insurance sector continues to strengthen its resilience
evidence.significance: FINMA's sector assessment keeps operational resilience in the same management frame as financial strength. Leaders should test whether a resilience claim is supported by accountable service maps, exercised recovery arrangements and evidence that remediation closes the underlying weakness.

leadRow.title: RESOLVED: We are investigating an issue where customers may experience timeouts, service degradations, errors, and elevated latencies across multiple products in the us-west1 region.

evidence.sourceTitle: RESOLVED: We are investigating an issue where customers may experience timeouts, service degradations, errors, and elevated latencies across multiple products in the us-west1 region.
evidence.significance: Google Cloud reported a multi-product us-west1 disruption caused by unexpected congestion during planned optical maintenance. Dependency mapping and scenario tests should extend below an application or availability zone to network capacity, restoration sequencing and provider communications.

evidence.sourceTitle: SEC Charges Former Executives With Fraud in Connection With $1.9 Billion Collapse of Subprime Auto Lender Tricolor
evidence.significance: The SEC alleges that Tricolor executives double pledged collateral and manipulated loan metrics in asset-backed offerings. leadRow.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog

evidence.sourceTitle: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
evidence.organisation: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
evidence.significance: CISA's latest Known Exploited Vulnerabilities update is an active-exploitation management signal, not a catalogue-reading exercise. Technology leaders need a complete asset view, a named exception authority, time-bound remediation and proof that the exposure has actually been removed.

leadRow.title: 26-140MR Rex held accountable for continuous disclosure failure, three non-executive directors did not breach duties | ASIC

evidence.sourceTitle: 26-140MR Rex held accountable for continuous disclosure failure, three non-executive directors did not breach duties | ASIC
evidence.significance: ASIC's Rex decision shows how quickly a forward-looking statement becomes a governance problem when the supporting information changes. Boards need clear thresholds for re-testing assumptions, escalating contrary evidence and recording why a market disclosure remains accurate and timely.
